Thanks Marissa — I reviewed the attachments. Summary and required steps from Procurements:

1) Vendor record & onboarding form: good. We need the completed onboarding PDF in our vendor portal (already attached by Krupesh).
2) Tax evidence: copy of VAT registration certificate (we have it) and a signed statement of tax residency is helpful but not mandatory for EU VAT handling. For non-EU vendors, we generally request a tax residency certificate if withholding exemptions are requested.
3) PO and invoicing: procurement will issue a PO once finance confirms tax treatment. PO should be referenced exactly on the invoice.
4) Tax treatment options:
   - If Redwood provides an EU VAT number and the supply is B2B, GDL can issue a net invoice under reverse-charge and we set vendor tax profile to "EU - reverse charge" in Netsuite (or internal AR/AP system).
   - If Redwood does NOT provide an EU VAT number (typical for US entities), vendor will charge VAT on the invoice; vendor must include VAT amount and registration number. Redwood will treat VAT as an expense (cannot reclaim EU VAT without an EU VAT registration).

Please confirm: Is Redwood paying from the US corporate entity (Redwood, Inc.) or via any EU affiliate? That determines whether reverse-charge is feasible. If there is an EU affiliate that can accept the invoice and provide a VAT number, that's often the easiest route to avoid VAT charged.

Next steps for Krupesh: please confirm which legal entity Redwood will route payment through (answer below) and whether you will charge VAT on the first invoice. Once Vivek confirms finance treatment, Procurement will issue PO and mark vendor tax profile.

Regards,
